name: Knowledge Graph Question Answering Leaderboard
description: Data-driven systems need to be evaluated to establish trust in the scientific approach and its applicability. In particular, this is true for Knowledge Graph (KG) Question Answering (QA), where complex data structures are made accessible via natural-language interfaces. Evaluating the capabilities of these systems has been a driver for the community for more than ten years while establishing different KGQA benchmark datasets. However, comparing different approaches is cumbersome. The lack of existing and curated leaderboards leads to a missing global view over the research field and could inject mistrust into the results. In particular, the latest and most-used datasets in the KGQA community, LC-QuAD and QALD, miss providing central and up-to-date points of trust. In this paper, we survey and analyze a wide range of evaluation results with significant coverage of 100 publications and 98 systems from the last decade. We provide a new central and open leaderboard for any KGQA benchmark dataset as a focal point for the community - https://kgqa.github.io/leaderboard. Our analysis highlights existing problems during the evaluation of KGQA systems. Thus, we will point to possible improvements for future evaluations.
evaluation_method: F1 / exact_match (per-dataset; many submissions report F1 as primary metric)
reputation: A broadly useful community-maintained leaderboard that aggregates KGQA results across many datasets and papers; referenced by KGQA researchers for comparisons and meta-analysis.
notes: Aggregates heterogeneous datasets with varying evaluation protocols; risk of inconsistent metric definitions across datasets and possible dataset contamination/duplication; not specific to LLMs (covers classical and neural KGQA systems).
